name: Bats

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Bats (bats1242).

notes: Research. Bats (Tsova-Tush) is a Nakh (Northeast Caucasian) language written in the Georgian Mkhedruli script supplemented by extra letters. The 33 standard Georgian letters take their usual phonemic values, including the ejective series; added signs write the schwa ჷ (ə), the pharyngeal ჺ (ʕ), the glottal stop ჸ (ʔ) and ჶ (f). Bats has a much larger consonant inventory than Georgian -- including pharyngealized consonants, additional uvulars, a voiceless-lateral series and nasalized vowels -- much of which is written with digraphs and diacritic combinations not resolved by this single-symbol map; those distinctions are left under-encoded, so a substantial PER floor is expected. Grapheme table checked against Holisky & Gagua (1994): no discrepancy found. Stress: Holisky & Gagua (1994) describe Bats stress as weak and dynamic but gravitating toward the word-initial syllable, occasionally shifting under morphological conditions the `stress` schema cannot express; `default_position=1` encodes the unmarked initial-stress tendency as an approximation, and the morphologically-conditioned shifts are a documented gap rather than silently wrong. The Georgian addition letter ჼ (Nar) marks nasalization of the preceding vowel by a synchronic rule described by Holisky & Gagua (1994, §1.4.5 'Nasalization'): a word-final (occasionally syllable-final) /n/ nasalizes the preceding vowel or diphthong nucleus and is itself deleted. The spec now encodes the majority, non-diphthong case as five vowel+ჼ digraphs (აჼ/ეჼ/იჼ/ოჼ/უჼ -> ã/ẽ/ĩ/õ/ũ), dropping wikipron PER from 0.3228 to 0.2790. In diphthong-final words the nasalization lands on the syllable nucleus rather than the trailing off-glide letter adjacent to ჼ (e.g. აუჼ realizes [ãu̯], not [aũ]); this residual ~6-word pattern is a documented gap, not fixed. The Georgian letter ჵ (Hoe), attested 13 times in the wikipron gold, is ambiguous there between the epiglottal stop /ʡ/ and the voiced pharyngeal fricative /ʕ/ (H&G describe /ħ/ and /ʕ/ contrasting only word-initially, and note Chrelashvili 1975 positing a third laryngeal /ʡ/); it remains unmapped by this spec rather than guessing a value the source does not settle, and measured folding of /ʡ/ and /ʕ/ out of the gold moves PER by under 0.001 -- a negative result, not a ceiling contributor. The wikipron gold additionally marks the voiceless lateral fricative /ɬ/ and voiceless pharyngeal fricative /ħ/ with a supplementary IPA modifier apostrophe that plain Mkhedruli, as attested in Holisky & Gagua (1994), does not write; this is folded in valid_ceiling.wikipron rather than fixed, since the practical orthography cannot recover it.

stress.notes: Approximates Holisky & Gagua (1994)'s initial-syllable stress tendency; morphologically-conditioned shifts to a later syllable are not expressible in this schema and are left as a documented gap.

wikipron.citation: Wikipron gold marks the Bats voiceless lateral fricative /ɬ/ and voiceless pharyngeal fricative /ħ/ with a supplementary IPA modifier apostrophe on top of plain Georgian letters (ლʻ, ჰʼ), a scholarly disambiguation the practical Georgian Mkhedruli orthography does not make -- confirmed against Holisky & Gagua (1994)'s grapheme table, which lists no such distinct letters. Folding /ɬ/->/l/, /ħ/->/h/ out of both sides drops wikipron/bbl PER from 0.2790 to 0.2635 (n=414); measured on fix/bbl-nasalization.
